Save a static plot

Source: R/plot_save.R
gtropic_save.Rd

Save a ggplot with ggplot2::ggsave(). This helper writes files; gtropic_plot() itself only returns plot objects.

Usage

gtropic_save(
  plot,
  filename,
  ...,
  dpi = 300,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  units = "in"
)

Arguments

plot

A ggplot, such as one returned by gtropic_plot().

filename

One nonempty output filename, optionally including a path. For static plots the extension selects the device unless device is supplied in ....

...

Uniquely named arguments. For static plots, passed unchanged to ggplot2::ggsave(), including device, path, bg, and scale.

dpi

Positive finite resolution in dots per inch. Defaults to 300.

width, height

Positive finite output dimensions in units, or NULL to infer them. Explicit dimensions are preserved. See Details for defaults.

units

Dimension units: "in", "cm", "mm", or "px". Pixel sizes are converted using dpi.

Value

Invisibly, the output filename, combined with path when supplied. The path is not normalized. Saver errors are propagated.

Details

Figure dimensions

Map plots carry a geographic gtropic_bbox attribute in the order c(xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) (named bounds may be in any order). The estimated width-to-height ratio is longitude span times the cosine of mean latitude, divided by latitude span. This is a geographic approximation, not a measurement of the final projected panels, legends, or facets.

Without usable bounds, the ratio is 7:5. With neither dimension supplied, width defaults to 7 inches and height follows the ratio. With one dimension supplied, the other follows the ratio. Inferred dimensions are bounded to 3–10 inches to keep narrow, polar, or very wide extents usable. Supplying both dimensions overrides all automatic sizing. Defaults are converted to the requested units.

See also

gtropic_plot(), ggplot2::ggsave()

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(mtcars, ggplot2::aes(wt, mpg)) +
    ggplot2::geom_point()
  output <- gtropic_save(p, tempfile(fileext = ".pdf"), width = 7, height = 5)
  unlink(output)
}
# }
